test_title: PYST 28: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 21 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following constitutional bodies was created to recommend appointments and transfers of judges in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Judicial Appointments Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) was established by the **99th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2014**.
 
• Its purpose was to create a transparent mechanism for the **appointment and transfer of judges** to the higher judiciary, including the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
• The NJAC comprised six members: the Chief Justice of India (CJI), two senior-most judges of the Supreme Court, the Union Minister of Law and Justice, and two eminent persons.
 
• The NJAC aimed to replace the collegium system, which had been criticized for its lack of transparency and accountability.
 
• However, the NJAC was struck down by the Supreme Court in **2015**, citing it as unconstitutional and violative of the independence of the judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collegium System:**

 
 
• The collegium system is a method of appointing and transferring judges of the higher judiciary in India, developed through Supreme Court judgments rather than legislation.
 
• It consists of the Chief Justice of India and four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court for recommending appointments.
 
• The system has been criticized for its lack of transparency and accountability.
 
 
 
• **99th Constitutional Amendment Act:**
 
 
• It was passed by the Parliament in 2014 to introduce the NJAC for judicial appointments.
 
• The amendment sought to enhance transparency and accountability in the appointment process.
 
• The Supreme Court declared it unconstitutional in 2015, restoring the collegium system.
 
 
 
• **Independence of Judiciary:**
 
 
• The concept ensures that the judiciary functions without interference from the executive and legislature.
 
• It is considered a cornerstone of democracy and is protected under Article 50 of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions for Judicial Appointments:**
 
 
• Articles 124 and 217 of the Constitution provide for the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts, respectively.
 
• The President appoints judges in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and other senior judges as per these provisions.
